Marathon Petroleum stock has inched up 0.44% today to close at $414.65, extending a strong three-day rally after recovering from a two-week slide. The move appears tied to structural strength in refining margins: US crude is trading at $89.62 per barrel while refineries are running at 95.2% capacity, and critically, heating oil prices have spiked 59% compared to last winter—a direct driver of demand and margins for refineries that produce these products heading into the cold season.

The broader backdrop has shifted meaningfully since early November. Russia's crude production recovery (which IEA data shows reached 8.73 million barrels daily in October) has pushed global oil markets from undersupply into surplus, which typically pressures crude prices downward—yet heating oil demand remains robust enough to support refinery profitability during winter months. This combination of abundant crude feedstock and seasonal heating demand is the kind of environment where refiners tend to thrive.
